db_evidence.notes: The true final-boss fight (a molten rock-and-fire giant, defeated ~75060-75090s) and its immediate post-fight equipment glance (75086-75090s, cursor on headpiece slot) and re-entry into gameplay (75140-75147s) are all present in the video and were retrievable via plain SQL scans of episodes/topic_facts (several rollouts' own run_sql calls, e.g. rollout 3 index 22 and rollout 4 index 41, actually returned these exact rows). However: (1) the textual episode/topic_facts summaries of this window describe it only as 'opens the equipment/inventory menu' or 'character development menu' and never name the equipped weapon or headpiece, so text-only retrieval cannot answer the question -- a clip_qa targeted precisely at 75086-75090s is required; (2) no rollout's clip_qa call actually covered [75086,75147] (closest miss: rollout 2's 74680-75060 window, 26s short); (3) a direct frame read at 75088s confirms the equipped headpiece text label reads 青铜猴面 ('Bronze Monkey Face', exact match to reference), and the equipped weapon icon (gold staff/monkey-face head) is consistent with 兽棍·金睛/降妖·金睛 ('Beast Cudgel · Golden Eyes'), which was forged/equipped earlier (~74490-74510s) and unchanged through the fight; (4) an earlier equipment/forging screen (~74400-74550s) shows a different, since-superseded headpiece (大力王面) being browsed/compared, which is what 2 of the 5 rollouts latched onto.

root_causes: Ambiguous 'final boss of chapter 5' identification: multiple visually similar boss-fight-plus-equipment-screen scenes occur between ~72000s and ~76000s (weapon forging at 73720/74400-74550, a golem fight at ~75000-75090, and another boss fight explicitly framed as 'the boss fight begins' at 75840), and rollouts scattered across all of them instead of converging on the one at the dataset's clue interval.

The DB's automatic text summaries (episodes/topic_facts) for the exact clue window (75086-75090s equipment glance) describe only generic menu navigation and never name the equipped items, so text-based retrieval (semantic_search, run_sql over text columns) cannot surface the answer directly -- a precisely-targeted clip_qa is required, and none of the 5 rollouts issued one that covered [75086,75147].

Two rollouts (2 and 4) got the weapon right by visually inspecting an earlier, textually rich forging screen (~74400-74550s) that explicitly names items, but that screen predates a later headpiece swap, so their headpiece answer is stale/wrong even though it came from a real, legible in-game menu.
One rollout (0) confused an accessory/curio (月玉兔, from the '珍玩' collectibles tab, visible at 75089-90s in the very same menu session) for a headpiece.

Rollout 3 had the correct SQL rows describing the true boss fight in hand but did not recognize/trust them (no explicit 'final boss' wording in the text) and instead issued clip_qa on a later scene whose text was more explicitly framed as a boss encounter.
what_worked: Broad SQL scans over episodes/topic_facts across the 74000-76000s range (rollouts 3 and 4) did surface the correct rows describing the true boss fight and its aftermath, showing the evidence chain is reachable by SQL alone.

Visual inspection of the ~74490-74510s forging/equip screen (rollouts 2 and 4) correctly identified the weapon name (兽棍·金睛 / 降妖·金睛), which matches the reference answer exactly and was stable through to the boss fight.
transferable_lessons: When a candidate time window is found via SQL/semantic_search but its text summary is generic (e.g. 'opens equipment menu') and does not name the items the question asks about, issue clip_qa on that exact window rather than substituting a different, textually-richer but temporally-distant scene.

For 'entity at time of event X' questions, verify equipment/state right at the event itself (immediately before/after), not at an earlier preparation/forging scene, since loadouts can change between preparation and the actual encounter.

When multiple similar boss-fight-like scenes exist in a session, prefer the one whose evidence best matches the dataset's temporal certificate/clue interval if available, or triangulate via the item names/state to see which slot values persist unchanged through to the fight rather than trusting the first 'boss fight begins'-labeled text.

Distinguish UI panel types (weapon/headpiece equipment slots vs. accessory/curio '珍玩' tabs vs. skill-tree/spirit-form tabs) before reading an item name off a menu screen -- multiple different menu tabs can appear within the same short window.
open_questions: Whether the dataset's clue-interval selection intended the 75088s equipment-tab glance specifically as the canonical evidence for both weapon and headpiece, or whether the weapon should instead be sourced from the earlier ~74490s forging confirmation (both are consistent with the reference answer, so this does not change the diagnosis).
